title: Diagnosing the Sources of Compositional Failure in Vision-Language Models: A Controlled Analysis

problem.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) often struggle with compositional reasoning tasks, but the reasons for this underperformance remain unclear.
statements: Vision-language models (VLMs) often struggle with compositional reasoning tasks, but the reasons for this underperformance remain unclear.
A common hypothesis is that models struggle to integrate multiple components, leading to training interventions to improve compositional binding.
However, this assumption has never been directly quantified.

limitations.summary: Compositional integration introduces a measurable cost, yet accounts for only part of the observed degradation; even models that handle joint reasoning well continue to suffer as caption complexity grows.
items: Compositional integration introduces a measurable cost, yet accounts for only part of the observed degradation; even models that handle joint reasoning well continue to suffer as caption complexity grows.
These findings reframe compositional failure as a multi-factorial problem in which joint reasoning accounts for only part of the observed degradation.
Several limitations point to directions for future work.
